subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a lava golem creature module in a Genshin-inspired toon style, using cel-shading and glowing lava seams, and sketching the skeletal rig starting with hips as the root joint before building out the spine chain.

Now I'm working out the full joint hierarchy -- legs, arms, neck, head, jaw, and fingers -- and designing a helper function to place basalt plate geometries relative to each bone. I'm sizing the figure at roughly 2.6m tall, calculating limb lengths and bend angles so the legs reach naturally from hips to feet, and setting up the spine as a catmull chain running from hips up through the chest.

Defining neck, head, and jaw placement...

Now I'm building arm chains with shoulder, elbow, wrist, then sprouting finger and thumb chains off the wrist joint for each hand, giving three fingers plus a thumb with two joints apiece and a "digit" role. I'm also planning the head/jaw geometry with glowing decal eyes via an SVG texture, and starting on the seam paint scheme for the basalt material.

Since basalt paint alone can't glow, I'm combining a cel-shaded crack pattern (using cell noise to detect crack edges and color them lava-orange) with separate emissive glow-rod parts placed between plates for actual light, writing the paint function to check the crack threshold and fall back to toon-shaded lit color otherwise.

Now I'm moving to the body geometry, lofting the torso along a spine bone chain with stations defining width/height at hips, mid-torso, and chest positions.

Adding torso glow ring, tilted rock plates on the back, a glowing icosahedron chest core with rock teeth, and vertical lava seam strips on the belly. For the head I'm shaping a blocky boulder with brow ridge, horn spikes, and glowing flame cards as a crest, plus a lava rock base platform.

Now I'm building that base as a dark basalt disc sunk to y=0.1 with glowing crack textures, making sure feet and hips align properly on top of it, and scattering small glowing rocks, crystals, and ember cones around a lava puddle disc near the base.

I'm setting up helper functions for mirrored body parts (left/right naming), flat-shaded geometry for rocky bits, and a glow wrapper for emissive lava-colored parts—then defining the foot as a flat box anchored to the ankle joint.

Now working out leg proportions: adjusting the foot's vertical offset so it overlaps the ankle properly, setting the hip-to-ankle distance and limb lengths to bend forward naturally, adding three small toe boxes, and sweeping the leg chain with a tapering radius. I'm also adding an icosahedron knee pad offset slightly forward from the knee joint.

Defining the hip joints symmetrically at x=±0.3, then laying out the arm chain with shoulder, elbow, and wrist points positioned outward and tapering forward, using a thicker radius profile for the forearm to match a heavy golem build, and planning a large blocky hand attached just below the wrist.

Working out finger placement as short two-point chains hanging off the hand, positioning each digit's base and tip to curl down and slightly forward so they read as stubby, dangling fingers on the fist.

Naming each finger as a digit with unique joint labels, then adding a shoulder pauldron using a scaled icosahedron plus a glowing torus ring positioned and rotated to sit horizontally around it.

For the back, I'm placing five plates along the spine, then adding basalt-column cylinders (hexagonal prisms) tilted and splayed across the back with glowing orange tips as a signature detail, reusing the column motif on shoulders and arms too.

Now defining a helper function that builds each column by aiming a cylinder along a direction vector and capping it with a thin glowing hex disc at the top. For the chest, I'm adding cel-shaded plates with a diamond-shaped lava core centered on the torso front surface.

Writing the ring of basalt spikes...

Now for the lava seams across the torso, I'm thinking of thin glowing rods connecting points down the chest, using a zig-zag polyline swept into a thin glowing tube with chest-anchored bones. I'm less sure about how the loft section's height axis should map onto the torso surface since the orientation along a vertical path feels ambiguous.

Safer approach: build the torso from scaled icosahedron primitives instead -- chest, belly, and pelvis each as flattened icosahedrons at different positions and scales, painted basalt, estimating where their front surfaces land based on vertex radius.

I think using a drape function against the torso parts would give cleaner seam placement than manually estimating surface points -- it pulls the polyline onto the nearest surface with a slight lift, and then I can sweep a tube along that draped path for the glowing seam effect.

For rigging, I still need a spine chain connecting chest, belly, and pelvis joints with parts rigidly attached rather than swept. Then I'm planning the neck and head: a hunched head joint angled forward from the chest, with a boxy skull shape and a small brow ridge box at the front.

Now I'm detailing the jaw and face: a jaw joint and lower jaw box with a glowing lava-orange mouth interior, small spike teeth on both jaws, and precise y/z positioning for the skull and jaw boxes so they align hunched forward.

I'm also working through the neck and chest proportions, trying to keep the head sitting naturally between shoulders without a visible neck gap -- adjusting chest scale and top height so the jaw and skull overlap correctly, bringing total creature height to roughly 2.9 units before horns or crown flames.

Now I'm positioning the eyes as small glowing yellow slit planes on the face, angled for an angry expression, and figuring out how to mirror the tilt correctly for the left and right sides using orientation vectors rather than separate textures.

I'm adding the brow as an angled box above the eyes, then working out the horns using curved spike geometry with a bezier sweep from base to tip, attaching them to the head bone and giving them an obsidian color.

I'm planning a flame crest using textured cards arranged in frames along the top of the head, plus a glowing rune disc placed on the base floor and a possible emblem texture for the chest core, keeping the total texture count modest around four or five.

Next I'm designing the base: a twelve-sided basalt cylinder with a ring of short hex-prism columns of varying heights around the edge, some capped with glow, plus the glowing rune disc overlaid at the center and floating ember particles as small glowing octahedrons scattered upward around the base.

For the arms, I'm adding small details like knuckle studs, elbow spikes made from backward-pointing columns, and a glowing torus band wrapped around the forearm oriented along the limb's tangent direction, sized just larger than the arm's radius with a thin tube and low-poly flat segments.

I'm applying the same torus treatment to the upper arm and legs, estimating radii based on each limb's sweep profile at different points along the chain, and sketching out a lava/Pyro-inspired cel-shaded basalt color palette for the armor plating.

Writing paint functions for cracks...

I'm thinking I'll restrict the crack texture to chest, pelvis, belly and arms rather than the whole body to avoid visual clutter, using a wider crack size for plain basalt plates like pauldrons, head, and columns. I'm also checking that `cells` and `noise` are properly exported from the paint module, while `cel` and `INK` come from the toon kit and `glow` from the glow kit, then setting up a seeded RNG for variation.

Now I'm building the skeleton hierarchy, starting with a hips root joint and a spine chain running through spine1, spine2, and chest, defining a side helper to label left/right limbs consistently.

I'm attaching the arms to the chest joint, then adding a neck joint and head joint with position and direction vectors defined in model-space coordinates.

Now I'm adding a jaw joint aimed at a point below the head, then sizing the skull as a box roughly 0.74 by 0.46 by 0.6, positioned so its bottom edge aligns with the jaw's top near y=2.36, letting the chest, head, and skull overlap slightly for a layered look. Still placing teeth geometry...

Defining more helper functions...

Still placing spikes and armor pieces...

Still defining leg chains...

Cones should point radially outward like rays around the core, floating near the chest surface at that depth. I'm bumping up the chest scale to [0.9,0.68,0.68] so the dodecahedron face sits around 0.64 at center and 0.78 at vertex, keeping the core icosahedron properly nested just inside.

Now I'm planning seam lines as draped polylines running symmetrically down the front of the torso, from chest to pelvis, which get resampled onto the nearest surface and then swept into thin flat-sided tubes. I'm also adding diagonal seams from the core up toward the shoulders for extra structure.

For the spinal back seam, I'll glow the swept mesh directly. Then I'm designing a rune disc texture — concentric rings and spoke-like glyphs drawn in SVG, placed on a circular geometry near the base, plus a simple eye SVG with a slit shape in a wide viewBox.

Writing eye SVG code...

Now designing flame-shaped SVG gradients, then planning crest card frames arranged along the head, varying position, angle, and size for a fanned-out decorative array.

I'm adding ember details as tiny octahedron spheres, then placing a base cylinder attached to the hips bone, weighing whether attaching props to a moving joint makes sense versus a fixed root.

Now I'm building the lava pool edge as a flat glowing torus ring, plus a ring of small basalt columns spaced around the base perimeter with varied heights and occasional glowing caps.

Fine-tuning cap placement to sit flush on the column top without z-fighting, then moving on to defining pauldrons using dodecahedron rock shapes attached at the arm joints.

Adding positioning details...
